body:
Jada Williams: Staging rollout update: we ran the first end-to-end on `staging-us-east-1` for `rollout-controller` auto-actions (flagged) against the `chat-completions` route. Canary stepped 1% -> 5% -> 10% successfully. Synthetic latency injection triggered auto-*pause* within ~6m. :thumbsup:

Jada Williams: High level: SLO evaluator -> policy engine -> audit event -> Console timeline all wired. No rollback execution in this pass (pause-only policy).

DeployBot: Deployed `redwood@a9c3f12` to `staging` (service: rollout-controller). (reactions: :shipit: x4)

Hannah Rivera: Confirming UI side: rollout detail page shows the “Auto action” row + detail panel. The “why” text is decent, but dashboard link is 404ing for me (looks like it’s missing `region` param).

Felix Schneider: Same. The event detail panel renders, but the link is pointing to `grafana/...&var-region=` (blank). Might be the label mismatch we saw earlier.

Caleb Johnson: Yep, metrics emitted `region=us-east-1` but the dashboard variable expects `cloud_region`. I can either update the dashboard var or add an alias label in the emitter (prefer dashboard update to avoid cardinality weirdness).

Aisha Bello: +1 on fixing dashboard. We should not add duplicate labels to the metric stream.

Chloe Martin: On Console API: `/api/rollouts/:id/auto-actions` worked, but we saw intermittent 500s when filtering by `time_window=last_1h`. I’m looking at logs now.

Chloe Martin: Log snippet:
```
error=invalid_time_window value=last_1h allowed=[15m,1h,6h,24h]
status=500
```
We should return 400 not 500. I’ll patch.

Ethan Park: Nice catch. That’s on the backend handler mapping. If you file a quick PR I can review fast.

Benji Okafor: Policy side looked stable. We used template `auto_pause_fastburn_v1`:
- fast burn: 5m
- slow burn: 30m
- min requests: 500
- debounce: 10m
No validation errors.

Jordan Lee: One issue: pause triggered twice on the same step. I saw two `DecisionOutcome=PAUSE` events ~20s apart with same `rollout_step_id`.

Jada Williams: Yeah I saw that too. Looks like step transition isn’t fully idempotent when the evaluator fires near the boundary of the step advancing.

Logan Wright: Telemetry side: we also saw two identical emits in event-stream. Might be upstream (controller) retrying vs us duplicating.

Incident Bot: FYI: Auto-action event posted to #eng-oncall (notify-only) for staging test. No paging. (reactions: :white_check_mark: x6)

Rafael Mendes: From the SRE viewpoint this was good: pause happened, and the Slack message had rollout id + dashboard link (even though link broke). No paging storms.

Sean Gallagher: +1. As long as prod stays notify-only initially and we have suppression controls, I’m good with expanding scope after the idempotency fix.

Jada Williams: I’ll open a ticket for the double-pause + likely lock around step transition. This feels like the same class as the earlier “double execution” risk.

Chloe Martin: For the 500, I’ll land a small fix in Console backend today.

Felix Schneider: Another tiny thing: audit event payload missing `policy_version` in one of the two duplicates. First event had it, second didn’t.

Benji Okafor: That’s probably because the second path is going through the default policy lookup (no resolved policy object) and then deciding. We should enforce `policy_version` as required in the audit event schema.

Ethan Park: Agreed. We should fail the decision emission if required fields are missing, or set it explicitly to `unknown` + suppression reason. But don’t emit partial.

Caleb Johnson: Re dashboard: I can patch `observability-pack` to use `region` var instead of `cloud_region`. Should be small.

Aisha Bello: Please do that. Also add a panel for “monitor stale/missing” even if we didn’t hit it in staging.

Connor O'Brien: Question for next step: are we comfortable expanding to one internal prod route behind flag after these fixes? Proposed: `prod-us-east-1`, internal customer tier only, route `internal-tools/chat` (low-ish volume but real traffic).

Sean Gallagher: Condition from SRE: 1) idempotency fix in controller, 2) Console 500 -> 400 fix, 3) dashboard link fixed, 4) alert routing remains notify-only and includes suppression if telemetry is degraded.

Jada Williams: Works for me. Idempotency fix is highest priority; I can land it tomorrow AM.

Chloe Martin: Console fix I can land today.

Caleb Johnson: Dashboard fix today as well.

Rafael Mendes: For rollout: can we also set a hard guardrail: no auto-pause if `min_requests` not met AND request rate < X? We don’t want a low-volume route causing weird behavior.

Jordan Lee: That’s already in policy template (min requests 500), but we can set `min_requests_per_window` too. I’ll check what the schema supports right now.

Benji Okafor: Schema supports `min_requests_total` across evaluation window; doesn’t do “per-window” yet. We can approximate by requiring both fast and slow windows to meet min. Not perfect but ok.

Ethan Park: Let’s not expand schema today unless it blocks prod test. I’d rather use existing knobs and iterate.

Connor O'Brien: Cool. I’ll draft the enablement checklist for the internal prod route and put it on the release train notes. Target: Friday, assuming fixes land by Wed.

Jada Williams: Decision: proceed with expanding to ONE internal prod route (notify-only, pause-only) once the three fixes are merged. I’ll post links to PRs here as they go up. (reactions: :thumbsup: x9)

Sean Gallagher: Thanks. Please tag me + Rafael on the PR that changes controller idempotency so we can sanity check failure modes.

Jada Williams: Will do.
